question: Is the reported LP2-15 extra interline gap measurable on the original JPEG, and how does it compare with local page-layout controls?

source_report.scope: The supplied discussion suggests both word gaps and line gaps as bits, but the original screenshots are unavailable. It specifically notes the gap before the final LP2-15 number row.

regions.role: lower rune-text control, red margin excluded
adjacent rune-text control, left drawing excluded

segmentation: Original 2400×3600 grayscale JPEG pixels, no resizing. A row is ink if at least five pixels in the fixed x-range have grayscale <160. Contiguous ink-row runs separated by at most 14 blank rows are one printed line. Measure blank rows from a line's last ink row to the next line's first ink row. No automated text/word parsing.
sensitivity: Repeat all four regions at gray cutoffs 100 and 200, keeping every other setting fixed. This is a threshold robustness check, not a model fitted to the outlier.
comparison: Report every line box and interline gap. Contrast the final numeric-panel gap against the panel's first two and the adjacent rune-text controls. Do not concatenate gaps into bits.
exclusions: No original forum screenshot coordinate can be inferred; word-space thickness, punctuation/fallback-font causation, page-wide binary decoding, and the intended purpose of LP2-15 layout are outside this test.
